prompt.context: Your client is Prescott Publishing, a major business media company. They have a wide range of product offerings, including general business magazines, industry trade letters and branded television programming. Performance has suffered recently, as print circulation has declined. The client leadership team wants to reboot their offerings with a new premium digital product. It wants to specifically target business executives with a paid web news offering.
prompt.question: They would like your help to understand the opportunity and whether you would recommend they go forward with an investment.

clarifying_info.q: What kind of product is it?
clarifying_info.a: The client wants to become the 'Home Page' of the modern executive, providing them with current insights and trends on their industry, deep subject matter expertise, and relevant data. It will be a premium product focused on revenue through paid subscriptions, with little if any emphasis on advertising.

clarifying_info.q: Do they know what price they want to charge?
clarifying_info.a: Review the competitive exhibit first and share your opinion. After you make an estimate, the client believes customers would pay $10/month.

clarifying_info.q: What does the company think defines 'an executive'?
clarifying_info.a: To the client, an executive is either someone in the top five leadership positions (CXOs), one of the top 6 direct reports to those positions, or one of their 6 direct reports (5x6x6=180 per company). They typically work for a large public company.

clarifying_info.q: What does the company expect it will cost?
clarifying_info.a: The company anticipates the construction and launch of the product would cost up to $30M, and would remain that significant going forward.

exhibits.title: Competitive Landscape
exhibits.shows: A table of five competitors with their pricing model and offering description

Wahoo.offering: Company financial reports; General Business News

Wealth Publishing.offering: Executive-focused lifestyle articles and general news

Woodson Research.offering: Customized research reports on specific industries/companies

framework: Market Size / Revenue Opportunity: estimate the total addressable market using target customer definition and subscription pricing
Potential Customers: size the executive audience using the client's definition (5 CXOs x 6 direct reports x 6 their reports = 180 per large public company x Fortune 1000)
Subscription Pricing and Other Revenue: benchmark against competitive landscape; anchor on $10/month ($120/year)
Costs: identify cost buckets — infrastructure, design, technical and reporting staff, maintenance, marketing; client estimate is $30M annually
Competition and Risks: free alternatives (Wahoo, Froogle), risk of price undercutting, low adoption outside target audience

questions.prompt: Based on the competitive landscape exhibit, what monthly subscription price would you recommend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note free options (Wahoo, Froogle) at the low end and $350/year research reports at the high end. Given the product description (premium but news/insights-focused, not bespoke research), the reasonable range is $75–$350/year ($6–$29/month). A strong candidate lands in the $75–$350/year band before being told the client chose $10/month.

questions.prompt: How large is the total addressable market for this subscription product?
questions.guidance: Use the client's executive definition and the Fortune 1000 as the company universe to derive the subscriber pool, then multiply by annual revenue per subscriber.

math.setup: Revenue per customer = $10/month x 12 months = $120/year. Customers = 5 (CXO positions) x 6 (direct reports) x 6 (their direct reports) = 180 executives per company x 1,000 large public companies = 180,000 potential subscribers.
steps: Total market size: $120 x 180,000 = $21.6M per year

questions.prompt: Should the client invest in this new digital product? What is the investment's breakeven?
questions.guidance: Compare the $21.6M revenue ceiling to the $30M annual cost. The product cannot break even within its defined target market. Breakeven requires 250,000 subscribers at $120/year, which implies targeting ~1,400 large companies — more than the Fortune 1000. Recommendation should be negative given the numbers.

math.setup: Breakeven number of subscribers = Total annual cost / Revenue per subscriber. Then convert back to number of companies.
steps: Companies needed: 250,000 / 180 executives per company ≈ 1,389 companies
Fortune 1000 only provides 180,000 potential subscribers — well below the 250,000 breakeven
math.answer: Breakeven requires ~250,000 subscribers (~1,400 companies), which exceeds the Fortune 1000 target universe. The product cannot break even in the defined market.

brainstorming.prompt: Given that the investment case is weak as structured, what levers could make the opportunity more attractive?

categories.name: Revenue enhancements
ideas: Higher subscription pricing (position more as premium research, closer to $350/year)
Advertising revenue (banner, native, or sponsored content — with care to preserve premium positioning)
Mobile app subscription tier or in-app purchases

categories.name: Market expansion
ideas: Broader targeting: small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs), not just Fortune 1000
Non-executive professionals who follow industry news
International executives in comparable large-company roles

categories.name: Additional value / new revenue streams
ideas: Executive networking platform or community features
Sponsorship of industry events or hosted roundtables
Data and analytics products sold to corporates (B2B licensing)
Podcast, video, or multimedia content to increase stickiness

categories.name: Cost reduction
ideas: Partnerships or content syndication to reduce original content costs
Platform-as-a-service infrastructure to lower build costs
Phased launch (MVP) to defer full $30M spend

recommendation: Do NOT recommend the investment as currently structured: the total addressable market of ~$21.6M per year is materially below the $30M annual cost base, meaning the product cannot break even within the defined Fortune 1000 executive audience.
The shortfall is structural, not marginal — the client would need to reach ~1,400 companies' executive ranks, exceeding the Fortune 1000 target universe.
risks: Free substitutes (Wahoo, Froogle) may cap willingness to pay and limit subscriber conversion
New entrants could further commoditize executive news content
High fixed cost base ($30M) creates significant operating leverage in the wrong direction if adoption lags
Premium brand positioning may constrain advertising revenue as a fallback
next_steps: Explore higher pricing options (e.g., $75–$350/year) more consistent with comparable premium offerings
Assess feasibility of broadening the target beyond Fortune 1000 (SMBs, non-C-suite professionals)
Model alternative revenue streams (advertising, events, data licensing) to close the revenue gap
Conduct a phased investment analysis: MVP launch at lower cost before committing the full $30M
